# Psalm 91 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Whoever lives under the protection of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.

**2** I will declare about the LORD: 'He is my safe place and my fortress — my God, and I trust him completely.'

**3** He will rescue you from every hidden trap and from every deadly disease.

**4** He will shelter you with his wings; you will find safety underneath them. His faithfulness will be your armor and your shield.

**5** You won't be afraid of terrors in the night or arrows flying during the day,

**6** or disease creeping through the darkness, or disaster striking at noon.

**7** Even if a thousand people fall beside you — ten thousand at your right — it won't touch you.

**8** Just open your eyes and watch — you'll see how the wicked are repaid.

**9** Because you've made the LORD your home — the Most High your dwelling place —

**10** no disaster will come near you; no sickness will approach your home.

**11** He will order his angels to protect you wherever you go.

**12** They will carry you in their hands so you won't even stub your toe on a rock.

**13** You will walk right over lions and cobras; you will stomp on fierce lions and deadly snakes.

**14** God says: 'Because he loves me and holds on to me, I will rescue him. I will protect him because he knows who I am.

**15** When he calls out to me, I will answer. I will be right there with him in trouble; I will pull him out and give him a place of honor.

**16** I will give him a long, full life and show him my saving power.'

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **91:1-2**: This is the most famous 'protection psalm' in the Bible. It's been carried into battle, whispered in hospital rooms, and prayed in every conceivable crisis. The core promise: being close to God is the safest place to be.

- **91:11-12**: These are the verses Satan quoted to Jesus during the temptation, trying to twist a promise of protection into a dare. The psalm is genuine — but it's not a magic spell. It's about trust, not testing.

— PNEUMA
